Eidz3t6qmk.text:
• Problem: feed-forward 3D reconstruction transformers scale past a billion parameters; depth may just buy implicit iterative refinement.
• Key idea: make iteration explicit by looping one shared transformer block K times over per-view DINOv2 features.
• Method: time-conditioned gated block with frame and global attention; depth, ray, and camera heads decode the final state.
• Training samples K from Beta(2,1) on [8,16], so one checkpoint exposes steps as an inference compute knob.
• Setup: 117M-parameter ViT-B model, 29 public datasets, evaluated on DTU, ETH3D, 7-Scenes, ScanNet++, and nuScenes.
• Results: best average IR (80.3%) and AUC@30 (91.8%) versus VGGT, Pi3, and DA3-G, using 75.9 TFLOPs and 4.9 GiB.
• New: shared weights beat untied per-step blocks (AUC@3 30.2 vs 23.0), but performance degrades well beyond 16 steps.

zSwgtp9S5a.text:
• Problem: web-scale pretraining hides prior exposure, so we can't tell whether interventions create or elicit capabilities.
• Key idea: constrain the training data itself to U.S. K–5 curriculum, creating an interpretable knowledge boundary.
• Method: AoA prefilter, LLM-judge-trained FastText/ModernBERT classifiers, symbolic filtering, and frequency sampling on FineWeb-Edu yield an 88B-token corpus.
• Validation: 0% Beyond-K–5 retained on CommonCoreText, 2.48% on WeeBit, 35–42% of K–5 retained.
• Setup: 5B Qwen3-style LittleLearner trained 100h on 8 B200s, compared to an Unfiltered twin and Gemma 2B.
• Results: matches Unfiltered on K–5 math; at Grade 8 pass@1024 it solves under half as many problems.
• Scaling, SFT+GRPO, and few-shot ICL boost in-scope skills but don't lift out-of-scope performance; the corpus and model are released as a sandbox.

69qwhyHQTB.text:
• Problem: glass surfaces mix near-field reflections with transmitted content, confusing single-set Gaussian Splatting geometry and rendering.
• Key idea: reflections are multi-view inconsistent, so residuals from fitting consistent content reveal transmissive surfaces.
• Method: dual 2D Gaussians (reflection plus scattering) composited by deferred shading, I = (1−R)·Iscat + R·Irefl.
• Three stages: fit scattering Gaussians, recover glass geometry from residuals, then train an MLP reflection light field.
• Setup: new 7-scene Blender dataset plus 4 real scenes, compared against 3DGS, 2DGS, Ref-GS, EnvGS and others.
• Results: transmissive normal error averages 7.46° versus 27.24° for the best baseline; best PSNR on all 11 scenes.
• New: first GS method to reconstruct curved transparent surfaces without geometry priors; fails when reflections are faint.

2MmzwEyeO2.text:
• Problem: robot datasets are human-absent, so trained policies lack human-aware behaviors like yielding, handovers, gesture following.
• Key idea: HABIT, 10,563 episodes, 164 hours, 60 bimanual tasks, always with a co-present human.
• Tasks span three roles: Collaborator (joint task), Coworker (shared space), Supervisor (human gestures direct robot).
• Protocol: subtask workflow graphs, reactive interaction, safety-first yielding, varied human speed, randomized gesture delays.
• Setup: two Franka arms, Quest 3 teleoperation, five cameras; π0.5 and GR00T N1.6 fine-tuned versus Robot-only baseline.
• Results: π0.5 Waste Sorting 40→65%, Box Packaging 50→85%, Food Storage 50→70%; collisions drop 60→0%.
• Mid-training on HABIT improves few-shot adaptation; Shelf Cleaning reaches 60% with 100 demos versus 45% direct.

VaoJb3PtWQ.text:
• Problem: VLM captions written for humans omit precise visual details that text-only math reasoners need.
• Key idea: reasoner clarification requests during training reveal information gaps, serving as implicit supervision for captioners.
• Method: tiered reward of 1 for direct success, 0.7 after clarification, 0 for failure, optimized with BNPO.
• Clarifications come from a frozen reference model; gradients flow only through the initial caption; inference is single-pass.
• Setup: InternVL3-2B or Qwen2.5-VL-3B captioner, frozen DeepSeek-R1-Qwen-32B reasoner, trained on ViRL-39K, seven math VQA benchmarks.
• Results: +4.4 average accuracy (39.0→43.4) for Qwen-3B, +10.6 DynaMath; beats binary-reward RL by 3.1 points.
• New: up to 39% fewer clarification requests; interface alignment learned from interaction alone, without caption annotations.

lj7OHtUYX1.text:
• Problem: identical numeric robot actions look different across cameras, placements, embodiments, breaking action-conditioned world models.
• Key idea: condition on a short visual calibration episode showing each motion DoF's pixel-space effect.
• Method: Wan2.2-5B DiT fine-tuned with calibration prefix, action-axis permutation/flip/scale augmentation, calibration-to-history distillation.
• Data: ~166 hours from RLBench, RoboCasa, RoboMimic with randomized cameras, plus DROID real-world data.
• Zero-shot on unseen LIBERO, ManiSkill, real xArm: PSNR 28.3/27.0/29.2 vs Ctrl-World 24.8/22.6/25.2.
• History-only mode nearly matches calibrated mode; best Met3R cross-view consistency on LIBERO and ManiSkill, near ground-truth bound.
• Training-free policy improvement via world-model ranking on LIBERO: e.g., Orange Juice 0.56→0.72 (oracle 0.80).

xMqv6BYsZv.text:
• Problem: embodied agents' changing memory contexts force full KV-cache recomputation each step, despite mostly unchanged content.
• Key idea: HeMeR treats declarative, procedural, and working memory as typed chunks mapped to KV ranges.
• Chunk-level reconciliation reuses unchanged chunks, recomputes affected ranges, and RoPE-remaps shifted chunks' cached keys.
• Adapter-stable reconciliation tracks LoRA adapter switches, recomputing only procedural chunks and dependents via shared-attention LoRA.
• Setup: ALFWorld (Llama-3.2-3B), Habitat (Qwen3-VL-4B), and real UR7e tabletop tasks versus MemRL, CacheBlend, KEEP, LRAgent.
• Results: ALFWorld 71.4% vs 52.9% SR; latency 0.18 vs 0.90 s/step; ~75% KV reuse.
• Real-world: 83.2% vs 64.3% success, 1.87 vs 2.94 s/step; first joint memory-content and adapter KV reconciliation.

mBYJRAFq7D.text:
• Problem: imagine-then-execute World Action Models pay heavy latency for iterative future video denoising at test time.
• Question: do WAM gains come from video co-training during training, or explicit future imagination at inference?
• Fast-WAM: Wan2.2-5B video DiT plus 1B action expert, Mixture-of-Transformer with shared attention, flow matching.
• Training jointly denoises future video and actions; masking blocks action tokens from attending to future frames.
• Inference: single forward pass over current frame only; 190 ms latency versus 580-810 ms for imagine-then-execute variants.
• No embodied pretraining: 91.8% RoboTwin, 97.6% LIBERO, close to Joint/IDM variants and pretrained LingBot-VA.
• Removing video co-training hurts most: RoboTwin 83.8%, LIBERO 93.5%, real towel folding drops to 10% success.
